meta.purpose: Reusable questions for school visits, heads and departments. Personal additions and answers are stored in private Openday state.

questions.ask: What is your current Progress 8 score? In practical terms, how many grade points does the school tend to lift pupils by compared with their starting points?
questions.why: Separates raw attainment from the progress pupils make while at the school.

questions.ask: What information do you give parents about academic progress, and how detailed is it? Do reports break progress down by topic or skill and identify specific areas where a pupil has difficulty or has not yet achieved mastery?
questions.why: Tests whether reporting is actionable rather than just a termly grade.

questions.ask: Could I see a sample timetable for a pupil in this year group? How many lessons per week or fortnight does each subject receive?
questions.why: Shows the real curriculum weighting and what pupils actually experience.

questions.ask: How much break and lunchtime do pupils have? What is structured or supervised, and how much genuinely free play or unstructured time is there?
questions.why: Reveals how much breathing space and independence exists in the school day.

questions.ask: Why should a child and their parents choose this school? What should they reasonably expect the school to deliver, and what do you believe a pupil should get out of the whole school experience by the time they leave?
questions.why: Forces a clear statement of the school's promise and priorities.

questions.ask: When assessment shows that a pupil has not mastered a topic, what happens next? How quickly is it identified, retaught and checked again?
questions.why: Distinguishes data collection from an actual intervention loop.

questions.ask: How do you identify and stretch pupils who already understand the core material without simply giving them more of the same work?
What is the typical homework load in Year 7, and how coordinated is it across subjects so several large tasks do not land together?
What does your behaviour system look like on an ordinary day? What are the most common sanctions, and what happens when a normally well-behaved pupil makes a mistake?
questions.why: Gets beyond slogans to the lived behaviour culture.

questions.ask: If a pupil is unhappy with a teacher, lesson or pastoral issue, how can they raise it and how do you make sure quieter children are heard?
questions.why: Checks psychological safety and routes for escalation.

questions.ask: For an enthusiastic orchestral instrumentalist who is still developing, what ensembles, lessons, performance opportunities and scholarship pathways are realistically available from Year 7?
questions.why: Separates opportunities for developing musicians from provision aimed only at already-advanced performers.

questions.ask: For music scholarships, what standard do successful applicants actually tend to be at, how do you weigh potential and instrument scarcity, and what commitment is expected after an award?
questions.why: Published minimums often do not reveal the real competitive standard or ongoing workload.

questions.ask: Apart from examination results, what outcomes do you track or care about when deciding whether the school has done a good job for a child?
questions.why: Surfaces priorities around independence, character, wellbeing and destinations.

questions.ask: What do parents most often complain about, and what has the school changed in response to parent feedback in the last couple of years?
questions.why: A concrete way to test openness and capacity to improve.
